ceilingSources.wakeupsPerSecond: design bound: the takeover monitor blocks on a condition variable with a one-second timeout (README Ranking row: a stat of takeover.json once a second, no faster polling; CHANGELOG 0.2.7 idle wake-ups entry), so 1 per second from the crate, doubled for the accept and shutdown paths: 2 per second. The 7.4 to 11.3 per second in the 0.1.5 evidence is the 25 ms sleep loop that entry removed
ceilingSources.residentMemoryBytes: rule: 2x the larger measured resident set (11206656 B over the recorded hosts), rounded up to a whole MiB; evidence runtime-budget.evidence/
ceilingSources.idleCpuPercent: rule: 1 percent absolute for an idle crate; measured at most 0.156 percent on the recorded hosts
ceilingSources.diskOpsPerSecond: rule: max(1, 2x measured) per second; Windows measured 0.0 (GetProcessIoCounters, all I/O including pipes); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter

status.note: The status call returns rightkit_child_process::ProcessUsage (resident and footprint bytes, cumulative CPU seconds, wake-up and disk-operation totals where the host reports them) beside the crate's own queue figures; the rates come from two calls (ProcessUsage::rates_since). Wake-ups are macOS and Windows only; disk operations are Windows and Linux only.
